newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army says it kills killers of archbishop.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army says it kills killers of archbishop.

text.p: The Burundi army said on Friday troops killed seven Hutu rebels from a group that killed Burundi's senior Roman Catholic prelate in an ambush.
An army spokesman said 50 soldiers clashed with rebels on Thursday at Gitongo, in the north of the central province of Gitega, where Archbishop Joachim Ruhuna and two nuns were killed on Monday.
"The rebels who attacked the soldiers are the same ones who killed the archbishop," said Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi, adding there were no army casualties and the rest of the rebels escaped.
"We are still trying to secure the area around the car. We haven't started searching for the body (of the archbishop) yet," said Nibizi, reflecting how little control the army has in some regions.
Four people with the archbishop survived Monday's ambush. A Burundian nun killed in the attack was buried on Wednesday but the bodies of Ruhuna and another nun have not been recovered.
Survivors said they were held hostage for more than 24 hours after the ambush.
Burundi's military government and the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD), the political wing of Burundi's main rebel movement, have blamed each other for the killings.
The CNDD says the army killed Ruhuna, who had received death threats after condemning extremists of both Burundi's Tutsi minority and Hutu majority and refused to travel with guards.
During the attack, Ruhuna's jeep smashed into a dirt bank a few hundred metres (yards) from the Mubarizi river. The vehicle was riddled with bullet holes and burned out, witnesses said.
The body of the 62-year-old archbishop was seen burning in the jeep shortly after the ambush but it later vanished. The army says Hutu rebels had probably thrown it into the river.
Nibizi said the army on Friday started a large operation to find the body and flush rebels out of the Mubarazi river area.
"This area is known for rebel activity. Mubarizi is in the middle of a valley that runs from Kibira forest to Tanzania," Gitega Military Governor Louis Muhengera told Reuters.

Bishop Bernard Bududira, the acting head of Burundi's Roman Catholic church, said he blamed Hutu rebels for the ambush. "I believe it is the Hutu rebels because that area is under rebel control," he said.
Eight Catholic priests have been killed in Burundi since 1993. More than 150,000 people -- most of them civilians -- have died in massacres and a vicious civil war between the army and rebels.
